name: dev-pod-pair
note: MEASURED 2026-11-26 with this scenario: pod A ends at rs=2 (`handback-wait {ms:10269, rs:2}`), the second pod`s DOM hold cancels it 877 ms later (`handback-wait-cancelled {ms:877, why:'ad-hold'}`) and its picture reveals, and the only `handback-ready` is pod B`s OWN capped exit 12 s later - so `rowsAtMost handback-ready 1` is the discriminating half: if the cancel had not run, A`s wait would have capped too and there would be two. TWO pods inside one hand-back wait: the native edge serves only init + one segment and then refuses native media for 30 s, so pod A ends with rs<3 and the wait arms; pod B's ad UI opens about a second later, and `ad-start` must CANCEL the wait rather than tear the replacement frame down (0.8.123, refuted limb: with the cancel removed, the next 150 ms poll computed !covered and killed pod B's frame). The `why` vocabulary is per PRODUCER: a DOM hold cancels with `why:'ad-hold'`, a worker `ad-start` (the `need-source` answer) with `why:'ad-start'` - both are the same single canceller. Timings are scenario knobs (midroll A 4-9 s, B 14-24 s): pod A's `ad-end` needs two clean playlist refreshes, which is what places the cancel one second into the wait.
